# Systemix

Systemix keeps your design system from rotting. It watches what you ship,
catches where design and code drift apart, proposes a fix with AI, you approve
it, and it remembers the reason — so your system gets sharper every release
instead of decaying.

## What it is

- A CLI and framework that automates your design system through a ship → signal
  → decide → record cycle. Every decision and experiment is a plain MDX file in
  your repo (hypothesis, evidence, decision, confidence), written back when a
  decision closes.
- Three doors into the same automation: Claude Code slash-command skills, the
  `systemix` CLI, or an MCP connector (`experiment_*` tools).
- Engine = your AI coding tool (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex). No extra service,
  no local model, no platform. The files are yours.
- Ghost mode by default: it suggests, never touches your code. Autonomy dials
  up to assisted or autonomous; a human always closes the decision.
- Evidence via PostHog (optional): wire it and headlines, CTAs, and flows
  become measurable evidence. The automation runs without it.
- Code-first tokens: CSS is the source of truth; a drift report shows where
  design and code split. Figma is an optional adapter.

## Getting started

- Free: `npx @systemix/cli init` scaffolds the automation (and optionally a design
  system) in your repo, ghost mode on.
- Full Kit (€99, pay once): the whole AI-native design-system context engine,
  downloadable — engine, docs, app setup, skills, and workflows. No
  subscription. https://getsystemix.vercel.app/kit
- AI-Readiness Audit (€249, emailed in 24–48h): send a repo URL, get back a
  scored readiness report — drift, slop, an opportunity ranking, and the
  exact setup to fix it. https://getsystemix.vercel.app/audit
